rows.grounds: compound: nandīśvara (Nandishvara) + anugrahaḥ (grace); grace of Nandishvara
fused particles: tu (but/and) + evam (thus); internal sandhi noted, token kept whole
comparative adverb indicating similarity to the preceding case
compound: viṣṇu (Vishnu) + prasāda (favor) + kṛt (causing/making); agent noun

items.question: What parallel divine graces are associated with the depicted form?
premises: The depicted form is associated with Nandishvara's grace.
The same form is likewise associated with causing Vishnu's favor.
Both associations follow the same manner indicated by the comparison.
items.inference: The described form corresponds to obtaining grace from both Nandishvara and Vishnu.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of these nominatives relative to the preceding imperative kuryād is implicit.
items.plain_english: Thus there is Nandishvara's grace, and likewise that which brings Vishnu's favor.
